title: Dream DAW open-source desktop workstation published on GitHub
summary: Dream DAW published its cross-platform digital audio workstation repository on GitHub, featuring a native audio engine written in Rust with a Tauri and TypeScript desktop interface.
research_notes:
Clone the repository from GitHub and install system dependencies including Rust, Node.js, and platform audio build libraries.

Build and run the Tauri desktop application to initialize the React user interface and native audio playback engine.

Provide an OpenRouter API key in application preferences to activate the AI assistant for track creation, clip editing, and chord generation.

Scan local VST2, VST3, and AU plugin folders or import existing Ableton Live project files into the timeline.

Host complex or unstable third-party VST and AU plugins in separate processes to prevent external plugin errors from crashing the main audio engine.

Keep audio fingerprint caching active during stem separation to eliminate redundant compute overhead on repeated audio segments.

Review assistant-generated MIDI notes and track structures prior to destructive timeline commits to ensure musical coherence.
